chunks: And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) laughed until his teeth were showing, then he said: 'Will you not ask me why I laughed?' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'I am amazed at the Muslim man; there is no decree that Allah decrees for him except that it is good for him in the end of his affair.'

key_terms.عَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِهِ: the end of his affair / outcome

ai.seo_question: Why is a Muslim amazed at their own fate according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the positive disposition of a Muslim towards divine decree (qada). The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) expresses amazement that whatever fate Allah ordains for a believer ultimately turns out to be good for them in the long run, reflecting the concept of 'good ending' (husn al-'aqibah).

en.muhajir-b-ali: 49. It has been narrated that Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) said:

' The Messenger of Allah (a.s) laughed once until his teeth were showing, 'Will you not ask me why I am laughing?' he asked. 'Indeed, O Messenger of Allah,' inquired the people. 'I am amazed at a Muslim, whatever Allah decrees for him will always turn out good for him in the end,' he said.
